subsystems.name: Fungal inoculum
subsystems.role: the living organism that grows through and binds the waste.

subsystems.name: Lignocellulosic substrate
subsystems.role: agricultural waste that provides the food and bulk of the panel.

subsystems.name: Mould and growth chamber
subsystems.role: shapes the panel and keeps conditions right for growth.

subsystems.name: Mycelium composite
subsystems.role: the grown material — a dense network of hyphae binding the substrate.

subsystems.name: Heat treatment and finishing
subsystems.role: stops growth, dries the panel and prepares it for use.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Agricultural waste is collected, shredded and pasteurised or sterilised to remove competing moulds and bacteria.

buildSteps.title: Inoculate the mix
buildSteps.detail: Fungal spawn is mixed with the waste, sometimes with a nutrient boost to speed colonisation.

buildSteps.title: Fill the moulds
buildSteps.detail: The mixture is packed into moulds, often with channels or inserts to shape the final panel.

buildSteps.title: Incubate
buildSteps.detail: Moulds sit in a warm, humid, dark room for days to weeks while the mycelium grows through and binds the substrate.

buildSteps.title: Demould and heat-treat
buildSteps.detail: The grown panel is removed and baked to kill the fungus, stopping growth and reducing moisture.

buildSteps.title: Finish
buildSteps.detail: Panels are cut to size, sanded, and may be coated or faced to improve fire, water or surface properties.

buildSteps.title: Install
buildSteps.detail: Finished panels are used as insulation or interior partitions, not as load-bearing structure.

prerequisites.tech: Fungal strains that grow on agricultural waste
prerequisites.why: many white-rot fungi readily colonise straw, hemp and similar residues.
sterilisation, inoculation and climate-controlled growing rooms are already used commercially.
mycelium composites must meet fire and durability standards before wider use in buildings.
untreated mycelium is hygroscopic and can degrade if wet, so coatings or treatments are needed.
current mycelium panels are not strong enough for primary structural roles.

pathway.milestone: niche insulation and non-load-bearing interior panels
pathway.unlocks: a carbon-negative alternative to foam and gypsum in some buildings.

pathway.milestone: improved fire, water and pest resistance through coatings and denser growth
composites with natural fibres or bio-resins for semi-structural panels
pathway.unlocks: use in walls, floors and furniture where some strength is needed.
construction that stores carbon instead of emitting it.
